history_is_authoritative_order: Chain order is this array, NOT the emitted_at stamps. Two sessions have now written stamps ahead of wall clock (ISA-008 at 02:05Z, the v0.2 pointer at 04:20Z) while ISA-009 carries the true 01:43:54Z. Immutable archives are not edited to reconcile clocks.
law: This pointer is mutable. The INSELFACTION it names is not. A correction appends a successor archive; it never edits a predecessor. `latest_inselfaction` names only the most RECENT transmission — it does not close, supersede or rank the others. Open authority items are enumerated in `open_items`, which is the field to read before assuming nothing is pending. Every source binding names its REPOSITORY alongside its commit, because a hash without a repository is not an address.
channel_invariants: INV-ISX-REVIEW-RESOLVABILITY — an INSELFACTION that transfers review authority MUST expose the reviewed source through a receiver-resolvable immutable reference. If the source chamber has no accessible remote: transport.review_status = BLOCKED_SOURCE_UNRESOLVABLE. This is a transport property and must not be recorded inside a source binding, where it reads as provenance.

INV-ISX-SOURCE-BINDING — a commit reference MUST name the repository it belongs to, and that binding must be verifiable in that repository. RUORA is many repositories; an unbound hash is not an address. Raised by ISA-009 after the v0.2 pointer described a conscious-conversation commit as a RUORA commit.

INV-E3-CANDIDATE-AUTHENTICITY — an adjudicator may confer E3 only when the candidate's detector event is reconstructable from its persisted source observations. Candidate metadata may identify a detection result; it may never prove one occurred.
INV-E3-COVERAGE-NO-RETROFIT — an evaluation example may not be used both to motivate a detector mutation and to independently validate that mutation.

INV-E3-CORPUS-MINIMIZATION — a coverage corpus may preserve only the content required to determine whether an observable E3 event occurred and whether the detector recognized it; privacy reduction must not alter the event-bearing language.
INV-CC-PILOT-SHADOW-DEFERRAL — no detector output may exist for a conversation before that conversation's transcript is frozen and digested. Causal order, not policy.

INV-CC-PILOT-BLIND-ORDER — labels for a conversation must be frozen before any detector output for that conversation exists, and a detector run must refuse until they are. Enforced from both ends: annotation refuses if a shadow record exists; shadow refuses until labels are frozen.
INV-CC-PILOT-SHADOW-INERT — the module naming the detector is unreachable from the session; a live session process never loads kernel.e3 at all.
INV-CC-PILOT-TRANSCRIPT-BINDING — a downstream artifact must carry its transcript's digest, and that digest must still verify against the transcript's own bytes.
INV-CC-PILOT-ANNOTATION-DEFERRED — the pilot may emit spans. It may not label them, partition them, or admit them to a cohort.

INV-SEALED-VS-BRANCH — a sealed verdict is a property of tagged history, derived from the sealed tree; branch revalidation is a property of one branch on one machine. Reporting them under one label lets an environment outage read as a loss of integrity.

INV-CC-QUOTE-ANCHOR — a quote is the byte-exact persisted verbatim of an ACTIVE episode supporting the TARGET signal; it confers no standing; and where no quote exists SELF emits a labelled reference rather than inventing one. QUOTE, REVELATION and PROBE never blur into one sentence.

INV-HBC-COMMAND-TRANSIT-SCOPE — captured command transit is not total execution causality. A transit record may witness declared/project-observable inputs, command streams, Git/tree conditions and filesystem deltas, but may not claim ALL_INPUTS, ALL_OUTPUTS or TOTAL_CAUSALITY without a separate containment model.
